data.name: Kalesh
data.gender_notes: Kalesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kalesh is a combination of two Sanskrit words: Kala, which means 'time' or 'god of time', and Ish, which means 'god'. Thus, Kalesh means 'God of Time' or 'God of Fortune'. In Hindu mythology, Kalesh is worshipped as the god of time, change, and fate. He is also believed to be the preserver of the universe. The name Kalesh carries the meaning “God of Time, Fortune” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Kalesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of time, fortune and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the cyclical nature of time and the power to change and adapt to new circumstances.
data.etymology: Kalesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Time, Fortune.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kalesh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Kalesh is a significant name in Hindu culture, representing the god of time and change. In Hindu philosophy, time is not a linear concept but a cyclical one, symbolized by the endless rotation of the cycles of nature and the universe. Kalesh embodies this aspect of time, reminding us of the cyclical nature of life and the importance of being present and adapting to change. Furthermore, in Hindu festivals and rituals, invocations to Lord Kalesh are often made to seek blessings for a long and auspicious life, emphasizing the role of divine will and the importance of living in harmony with the cycles of time.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kalesh signifies the all-encompassing and eternal nature of God. As the god of time, Kalesh is believed to witness and oversee all aspects of creation, preservation, and destruction. He represents the inherent unity and interconnectedness of all things in the universe, reminding us that everything is part of the divine plan and that each moment is a manifestation of God's will. Additionally, Kalesh reminds us of the impermanence of material existence and the importance of living in the present moment, surrendering to the divine will and focusing on spiritual growth and wisdom. Ultimately, Kalesh represents the idea that God is not limited to any one form or manifestation and is present in every moment, reminding us to seek and find the divine in all things.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kalesh symbolizes the eternal dance of time and the transient nature of material existence. The name is derived from Kala, the Hindu god of time, andesh, the impermanence of all things. It serves as a reminder to cherish the present moment and find joy in the ever-changing tapestry of life.
